entries.title: EU herbal monograph: St John's wort herb (Hyperici herba), revision 1
entries.finding: The EU herbal medicines committee (HMPC) accepts certain St John's wort preparations for mild to moderate depressive episodes as a well-established use. It also lists several traditional uses based on long-standing use: temporary mental exhaustion, minor skin inflammation and wounds, mild digestive discomfort, and nervous restlessness with trouble falling asleep, each for specific preparations.
entries.limitations: The monograph covers defined herbal preparations used as medicines, not picking or preparing the plant at home, and the traditional uses rest on long-standing use rather than clinical trials. The committee does not recommend use under 18 years, and safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established.
entries.preparation: Defined herbal preparations: dry extracts, liquid preparations and herbal tea, depending on the use
entries.design: Expert committee (HMPC) assessment of the literature and long-standing use, in well-established and traditional-use categories
entries.safetyNote: The EU monograph says St John's wort must not be combined with several prescription medicines, including coumarin-type blood thinners, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, some HIV medicines and some cancer medicines. It also warns of interactions with antidepressants (very rarely a serotonin syndrome), with hormonal contraceptives (which may become less reliable) and before surgery, and advises avoiding intense UV exposure. Anyone taking prescription medicines is advised to ask a doctor or pharmacist first.

entries.title: Cochrane review: St John's wort for major depression (Linde et al., 2008)
entries.finding: A review of 29 randomised, double-blind trials with 5,489 people with major depression found that St John's wort extracts did better than placebo and about as well as standard antidepressants, and that fewer people stopped them because of side effects. The placebo-controlled results varied widely between trials.
entries.limitations: The authors note that trials from German-speaking countries reported more favourable results, which complicates interpretation. The review dates from 2008, covers only the extracts tested in those trials, and some authors declared past ties to a manufacturer.
entries.preparation: Extracts of St John's wort; the specific extracts differ between trials
entries.design: Systematic review with pooled results of randomised, double-blind trials (Cochrane)
